method: Derived (not measured on the wire) from the committed mcp/eval/slice15-eval-pairs.json tool_call fields. For each of the 10 pairs the request is reconstructed exactly as mcp/eval/run-eval.ts and tools/slice16-harness/mcp-client.mjs send it, then measured with Buffer.byteLength(..., "utf8").

serialization.primary_definition: JSON.stringify({jsonrpc:"2.0", id, method:"tools/call", params:{name, arguments}}) — compact (no whitespace), key order as written, UTF-8 bytes. This is the exact newline-delimited line written to server stdin; the trailing newline is NOT counted.
serialization.id_caveat: id is assigned 2..11 (0=initialize, 1=tools/list), mirroring tools/slice16-research/measurements/measure-envelopes.mjs. Ids 10 and 11 are two digits, so those lines carry 1 extra byte. The id is part of the wire payload and is therefore counted.

secondary_definitions.params_object_bytes: JSON.stringify({name, arguments}) — id-independent, the tool call proper.

serialization.median_convention: For even n, the mean of the two central order statistics — the same convention used by envelope-payload-sizes.json.

discrepancy_note: A prior chat-reported figure of min/median/max 127/202/297 B was cited as house-measured request sizes. It does not reproduce under any serialization derived here (closest is jsonrpc_line_bytes at 105/121.5/253) and no such measurement exists anywhere in the repo. The 127/202/297 figures are therefore NOT adopted; the values in this file supersede them. No transformation reconciling the two was found, and none was manufactured.
relation_to_est_tok: est-tok elsewhere in Slice 16 remains a labeled chars/4 heuristic, never a tokenizer count. No est-tok figure is derived in this file: request payloads are small relative to the 20,753 B tools/list prefix and do not change the order of magnitude of the cost model.
